questions.question: Which of the following is a common physical or visual indicator that a chemical reaction has taken place?
options: The mixture remains completely unchanged in appearance and temperature.
A change in colour, bubbling, or a change of temperature occurs.
The total volume of liquid increases without any other changes.
The container becomes instantly heavier without adding anything.

questions.question: What happens to atoms during a chemical reaction to create new substances?
options: They are destroyed and replaced by completely new elements.
They rearrange themselves into different combinations.
They turn into energy and disappear from the system.
They merge together to form one giant, single atom.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally true about chemical reactions?
options: They can always be easily reversed by cooling the mixture.
They are generally irreversible.
They never produce any new chemical substances.
They only happen when substances are frozen.

questions.question: What three components are necessary to initiate a combustion reaction?
options: Fuel, carbon dioxide, and water
Fuel, nitrogen, and a catalyst
Fuel, oxygen, and an initial source of energy like heat
Fuel, hydrogen, and high pressure

questions.question: Under what conditions is water often formed as a product in a chemical reaction?
options: Only when nitrogen and oxygen atoms are present in the reactants.
When hydrogen and oxygen atoms are present in the reactants.
When carbon and hydrogen atoms are heated in a vacuum.
Only when water is used as the solvent for the reaction.

questions.question: Why are carbon dioxide and water very common products in many chemical reactions?
options: They consist of large, complex polymers that decompose slowly.
They consist of small molecules that form easily with strong bonds.
They are the only substances that can contain oxygen.
They have weak bonds that break apart at room temperature.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a decomposition reaction?
options: Two elements combine to form a single, larger compound.
A single compound breaks down into two or more products.
An insoluble solid forms when two clear solutions are mixed.
Oxygen reacts with a metal to form a metal oxide.

questions.question: What are the typical products when a metal carbonate is heated and undergoes decomposition?
options: A metal and pure oxygen gas
A metal oxide and carbon dioxide gas
Hydrogen gas and a metal hydroxide
Carbon monoxide and water vapour

questions.question: What is the scientific term used when a substance reacts and combines with oxygen?
options: Reduction
Decomposition
Hydration
Oxidation

questions.question: Which of the following processes are both examples of oxidation?
options: Combustion and rusting
Thermal decomposition and neutralization
Melting and evaporation
Filtration and precipitation

questions.question: What defines a precipitation reaction when two solutions are mixed together?
options: A gas is rapidly released with a loud pop.
The solutions turn into a single solid block of ice.
An insoluble solid is formed from the combination.
The temperature of the mixture drops to absolute zero.

questions.question: Why are precipitation reactions practically useful in municipal water treatment?
options: They increase the oxygen level in drinking water.
They help to dissolve solid plastic waste.
They are used to remove unwanted substances from water by forming solids.
They turn the liquid water into a steam phase for distillation.

questions.question: How does the total mass of the products in a chemical reaction compare to the total mass of the reactants?
options: The products always have a much higher mass than the reactants.
The products always have a lower mass because atoms are destroyed.
The mass of the products is exactly the same as the mass of the reactants.
The mass changes unpredictably depending on the temperature.

questions.question: What information is represented by a chemical formula?
options: The speed at which a chemical reaction occurs.
The physical state (solid, liquid, or gas) of the substance.
The numbers of each type of atom in a reactant or product.
The cost and availability of the chemicals used.

questions.question: What does the arrow represent in a written chemical equation?
options: ‘changes into’
‘is equal to’
‘reverses back to’
‘dissolves in’
